title: Preflight passes an out-of-range dependency (#1828) — does diagnosing-bugs change the fix?

traps.why: The skill's Phase 4 tags every probe `[DEBUG-xxxx]` and its Phase 6 greps them out. One left in the diff is the skill followed halfway.
A tell only. The skill's last-resort human-in-the-loop script. This bug reproduces with one `mv` and one command, so reaching for it is a loop built for the wrong case.
A tell only. The preflight's header says it has no dependencies because it runs before anyone has a working install; a `semver` dependency would need the install it checks.
Criterion 2, and the skill's Phase 5: a test of the fault lands with the fix. Any new test case under tools/ counts, so an arm is not graded on the landed file name.

Criterion 1, as a backstop. Presence cannot tell r169 from r187; only the resolved package.json's version can. The pattern is the bare word, because the landed fix destructures `({ version } = readJson(found))` and a `.version` pattern failed it. The repro itself, re-run on the arm's tree, is the real check.

Criterion 2's second half. A tell, not required: a test placed under a directory `test:tools` already globs runs with no script line, so a trip here is checked by hand against the arm's tree before it is recorded.
